content.text: : neutralize existing gastric acid & raise the pH within the stomach & the duodenal bulb, stimulates restitution of the gastric mucosa, stimulation of PG production & release for cytoprotection, inhibit conversion of pepsinogen to pepsin
: used on a PRN basis to provide symptomatic relief of ulcer pain & dyspepsia
: formation of CO2 results in gastric distention & belching
Caution in HTN, CHF, CKD, cirrhosis
: constipation, aluminum accumulation in renal dysfunction (osteodystrophy, osteomalacia, encephalopathy)
: non-absorbed, locally-acting agent that binds to and protects ulcerated tissue from acid, pepsin, and bile salts
: short-term management (up to 8wks) of active duodenal ulcer; maintenance therapy for duodenal ulcer after healing of acute ulcers
: H2 receptor antagonists selectively and competitively inhibit the actions of histamine at the H2 receptors
: active duodenal ulcer, maintain healed duodenal ulcer, GERD, active benign gastric ulcers, maintain healed gastric ulcer, hypersecretory state (ZES)
•IV doses: CNS effects – confusion, delirium, slurred speech, hallucination
: irreversibly binds to the H-K ATPase and inhibits basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion (most potent acid suppressive agents)
Maximal acid suppression occurs when the PPI is taken 0.5-1hr before a meal
: DOC for treating PUD, GERD, & ZES
: C. diff-associated diarrhea, osteoporosis related fractures, vitamin B12 deficiency (prolonged use), acute interstitial nephritis, cutaneous & systemic lupus erythematous
: DA antagonist; enhances the response to Ach in the upper GIT, causing enhanced motility, accelerated gastric emptying, and increases LES tone
: PUD – commonly used when pts have coexisting gastroparesis; not recommended for GERD
